## Description

<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:BEGIN -->
Feature parent for the ODOC-63.2 JIT feature-wayfinding campaign: deliver the complete confirmed Quest side of Quest/Lore/Backlog tracker parity — a public schema-1 task projection with full CLI/manifest coverage, create/edit/list/view/search/status-flow semantics, and a lossless multi-pass Backlog task/milestone migration (aliases, configured vocabularies, digest-bound preview/apply/status/rollback, resumability/idempotency, relationship closure, source immutability). Lore-owned knowledge adoption and archive/delete are out of scope; publication is a later campaign. Grounding: opum-doc dev merge 995b966e8a2bb044c94b5defccbeb06f6cf89c85 (docs/stories/ship-the-lore-and-quest-tracker-parity-release.md, docs/specs/lore-quest-tracker-parity-adoption-and-paired-release-architecture.md, docs/adr/keep-lore-as-documentation-authority-and-quest-as-task-authority.md); canonical adapted capability at opum-doc .treehouse/opum-doc-811ba3/3/opum-doc/tooling/codex-skills/feature-wayfinding/SKILL.md (read-only).
<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:END -->

## Acceptance Criteria
<!-- AC:BEGIN -->
- [ ] #1 A local feature parent exists with sharp child issues created through Backlog CLI and native dependencies wired before execution
- [ ] #2 The public schema-1 task projection and CLI/manifest cover IDs/aliases/lifecycle/status, title/description, labels/assignees, priority/type/ordinal/dates, parent/dependencies/milestone with atomic forward/back references, ordered checked AC/DoD, plan/notes/comments/final summary, references/modified files, and Lore documentation references only
- [ ] #3 Create/edit/list/view/search/status-flow semantics include replace/add/remove/clear, deterministic ordering, case-insensitive configured statuses, actor-required atomic writes, stable versioned JSON diagnostics, and fail-loud compatibility
- [ ] #4 Lossless multi-pass Backlog task/milestone migration preserves aliases and configured vocabularies with digest-bound preview/apply/status/rollback, resumability/idempotency, relationship closure, and source immutability; no Lore-owned knowledge adoption or archive/delete is implemented here
- [ ] #5 Focused tests, full repository checks, installed-package/packaging validation, strict Lore gates, and exact-tree two-axis review pass before PR to dev
<!-- AC:END -->

JIT DAG: .1 reconcile -> .2 schema/projection/manifest contract -> .3 CLI semantics -> .4 migration mapping/provenance/closure -> .5 qualify/review/deliver.

Root cause: this task migrated in from Backlog already In Progress with no lifecycle event recorded, so the state machine has no history to demote from. Filed as a quest-cli defect (see linked task) rather than working around it by editing .quest/ directly. Status remains In Progress pending a fix.

This is the first live use of quest task pause for the purpose that motivated building it (QCLI-229): restoring this repository to exactly one In Progress task so the opum-workflow session-end hook can write to it again.

CAVEAT recorded 2026-09-09, not to reopen this closure but so a later reader does not repeat the inference: this task's closure reasoning cited 'status Blocked with an empty blockers array' as part of the evidence it was a stale migration artifact. That reasoning was flawed, though it did not change the outcome here. lore-cli and the orchestrator (opum-agent) found that Quest's blockers field has NO CLI write path at all -- confirmed independently (QCLI-251) -- so every Blocked task in every Quest workspace has an empty blockers array by construction, whether or not it is genuinely blocked on something real. The empty array was never evidence of anything. This closure's actual evidence stands independently: the task's own 2026-09-07 note already recorded its scope as superseded by the Backlog->Quest cutover, and all five children (QCLI-197/198/199/202/203) were Done. See QCLI-251 for the tracked defect.
finalSummary:
Closed as a stale migration artifact. QCLI-196 (alias QCLI-97.11) sat at status Blocked with an empty blockers array while all five of its children were already Done: QCLI-197, QCLI-198, QCLI-199, QCLI-202, QCLI-203. No open blocker or dependency behind it -- confirmed by the orchestrator (opum-agent, wave 3 close-out) and by inspection: an empty blockers array cannot itself hold up a status, and every piece of child work this feature parent decomposed into had already landed. This is the kind of stale status a human would have to read the children to disbelieve, which is why it survived past the migration. Closing on that evidence rather than any remaining open acceptance criterion on this record itself.

Consistent with the task's own recorded history: a 2026-09-07 note already documents this task's scope as superseded by the Backlog->Quest cutover (QCLI-160/169) and quest 0.3.4-0.4.0, and that it was parked at Blocked via quest task pause -- a workaround for a since-fixed lifecycle-transition bug (this task migrated in from Backlog already In Progress with no lifecycle event to demote from), not an indication of live blocking work. The five acceptance criteria on this record (local feature parent, schema-1 projection, CLI semantics, migration, and qualification/review) map to the work actually delivered and closed through QCLI-197, QCLI-198, QCLI-199, QCLI-202, and QCLI-203, so they are left unchecked here rather than checked on a record they were superseded on.
